messages:
cheng: Heads up — multiple tenants reporting stuck SSE streams after the routing change this morning. Clients show no new events and never reconnect.
eli: Confirmed. Proxy logs show client side 408/timeout but backend kept the session alive (no session_end). Looks like our keepalive->drain transition didn't close the opaque session.
marta: Console shows a big jump in resume attempts for t-42 and t-99, but resume_token mismatch errors in backend. Possibly stale token persisted at proxy layer. :eyes:
sam: Pasted a snippet.
```
proxy: keepalive timeout expired for session=abc123 route=eu-west
backend: session marked active tenant=t-42 session_id=abc123 last_seen=2025-04-12T09:12:03Z
proxy: attempted resume request id=abc123 -> 401 invalid resume_token
```
cheng: The important bit is proxy didn't emit session_closed so autotagger/quotas didn't decrement. Tenants are getting charged for a session that never receives tokens.
marta: That matches billing complaints. We saw a small uptick in token_cost anomalies starting at the rollout timestamp.
eli: Root cause hypothesis: new routing policy introduced a sticky-lease grace period that keeps session state in upstream for X secs expecting client reconnect. But our proxy's keepalive was shorter, so we get timeout + resume race.
sam: Proposed hotfix: 1) force emit session_end on proxy timeout to ensure quotas decrement; 2) add a short backoff window before attempting resume so token can be reclaimed; 3) instrument resume_token lifecycle in console.
cheng: I like forcing session_end. But careful: some clients rely on resume window (mobile). We should gate hotfix to non-mobile routes or tenants.
marta: Console UX item: add 'in-flight sessions' per-tenant and a small 'resume window' slider (5s/30s/60s) so SREs can tune. Also expose resume_failure_rate metric.
sam: Quick experiment idea: instead of forcing session_end globally, emit session_end + add metadata session_closed_reason=proxy_timeout to allow downstream to decide whether to bill. That keeps auditing.
eli: Agree on metadata. Also we need a migration plan for billing: ephemeral sessions between proxy timeout and backend reclaim might have been double-counted. ops-oncall @ops-oncall can you check if we need credits issued?
ops-oncall: On it — I'll pull top 20 tenants with highest in-flight counts and pause automated billing until we verify.
deploy-bot: Starting a canary rollback of the routing policy to v2.7 for 10% of traffic now. (canary id c-194) :gear:
cheng: We'll also add a tiny change in the proxy: when keepalive triggers, write session_closed_event immediately and mark session.draining=true for N seconds, so resume attempts within that N seconds are treated as valid resumes but quotas already decremented.
marta: Can we add a console alert for resume_token_mismatch spikes? Feels like an early-warning signal.
sam: Filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 — contains proxy change + metric. Please review.
eli: One more telemetry ask: tag resume_attempts with route_hash and tenant_id so we can correlate with routing policy rollouts.
cheng: Agreed. Action items: sam -> land PR behind a feature flag; deploy-bot -> rollback canary to v2.7 (in progress); ops-oncall -> pause billing check; marta -> console mock for resume window slider; eli -> add resume_attempts routing tags.
marta: I'll mock the slider in the console tomorrow and add a follow-up with screenshots.
sam: If we can push the proxy flag change and emit session_closed_event, we should see immediate drop in stuck sessions.
ops-oncall: I'll post the tenant list & billing hold in #finance once I have it.
cheng: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after canary rollback telemetry stabilizes. :thumbsup:
